title: Grateful Dead Live at Santa Clara County Fairgrounds on 1968-05-18

ai_review.summary: A gritty audience tape that still captures a blistering Alligator‑Caution‑Feedback run with Jerry’s electrifying guitar and wild Pigpen organ.
ai_review.review: This 1968 audience recording is rough around the edges – muddy, oversaturated and occasionally clipped – but it delivers one of the most ferocious early‑68 sets ever captured.  The highlight is a soaring Alligator → Caution → Feedback sequence punctuated by mind‑blowing drums and Jerry Garcia’s pure electric intensity.  Despite its sonic flaws the performance shines so brightly that listeners repeatedly call it a “lost gem” in Dead history.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for the musical performance (standout Alligator, Caution, Feedback) outweighs the moderate recording quality; weighted average yields ~4.4 stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Grungy, rough and muddy with on‑stage mic oversaturation, some hiss, occasional clipping and barely audible Pigpen vocals, but considered as good as any 1968 audience tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Short, high‑energy set with fluid transitions; the Alligator → Drums → Jam → Alligator reprise and the Alligator → Caution → Feedback sequence are repeatedly highlighted as peak moments.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as 'pure electricity' on Alligator with perfect tone and unstoppable energy.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s incendiary ‘proletariat’ rant is a memorable moment; Pigpen’s organ screaming is noted, though his vocal is hard to hear.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ keys are bashing and wild; his vocal barely cuts through the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drums are called 'mind‑bending' and a major highlight of the performance.
